name: 詹姆斯·克拉克·麦克斯韦

points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 詹姆斯·克拉克·麦克斯韦于1831年6月13日出生于爱丁堡的贵族家庭。他的父亲是苏格兰律师，家族拥有广泛的地产资源。麦克斯韦童年时期展现出非凡的智力，8岁时母亲去世，由父亲和姐姐抚养。这段时期他接受了早期教育，对自然现象表现出浓厚兴趣，尤其痴迷于几何学和机械装置。父亲鼓励他的科学探索，为他提供了丰富的书籍和实验设备，这为他后来的科学研究奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: James Clerk Maxwell was born on June 13, 1831, in Edinburgh to a noble family. His father was a Scottish lawyer with extensive estate holdings. Maxwell showed exceptional intelligence from an early age. When his mother died when he was eight, he was raised by his father and sister. During this period, he received early education and developed a keen interest in natural phenomena, particularly fascinated by geometry and mechanical devices. His father encouraged his scientific explorations, providing him with abundant books and experimental equipment, which laid the foundation for his later scientific research.

points.title: 大学启蒙
points.description: 1847年，16岁的麦克斯韦进入爱丁堡大学学习。在这里，他系统学习了数学、物理和哲学等课程，展现出卓越的才华。他发表了第一篇科学论文《论弹性固体的均衡》，探讨椭圆曲线的绘制。这段时期，麦克斯韦不仅掌握了扎实的科学知识，还培养了独特的思维方式。他善于将抽象的数学概念与物理现象联系起来，这种思维方式成为他后来科学研究的特色。爱丁堡大学的教授们对他的才华印象深刻，鼓励他继续深造。
points.descriptionEn: In 1847, at the age of 16, Maxwell entered the University of Edinburgh. Here, he systematically studied mathematics, physics, and philosophy, demonstrating exceptional talent. He published his first scientific paper 'On the Equilibrium of Elastic Solids,' exploring the drawing of oval curves. During this period, Maxwell not only acquired solid scientific knowledge but also developed a unique way of thinking. He excelled at connecting abstract mathematical concepts with physical phenomena, a thinking style that became characteristic of his later scientific research. His professors at the University of Edinburgh were impressed by his talent and encouraged him to pursue further studies.

points.title: 剑桥深造
points.description: 1850年，麦克斯韦转入剑桥大学三一学院学习，这是他学术生涯的重要转折点。在这里，他受到了著名数学家威廉·霍普金斯和爱德华·劳斯的影响，数学能力得到极大提升。1854年，他以数学荣誉学位考试第二名的优异成绩毕业，并获得了史密斯奖。在剑桥期间，麦克斯韦开始深入研究电磁学，阅读了法拉第的实验研究，并尝试用数学语言描述这些现象。这段经历为他后来统一电、磁、光的理论奠定了基础，也培养了他将实验与理论相结合的研究方法。
points.descriptionEn: In 1850, Maxwell transferred to Trinity College, Cambridge, where he studied, marking a significant turning point in his academic career. Here, he was influenced by renowned mathematicians William Hopkins and Edward Routh, greatly enhancing his mathematical abilities. In 1854, he graduated with second-class honors in the Mathematical Tripos and won the Smith Prize. During his time at Cambridge, Maxwell began to delve into electromagnetism, reading Faraday's experimental research and attempting to describe these phenomena using mathematical language. This experience laid the foundation for his later theory unifying electricity, magnetism, and light, and also cultivated his research method combining experiment with theory.

points.title: 早期教职生涯
points.description: 1856年，麦克斯韦被任命为阿伯丁马里沙尔学院的自然哲学教授。在这里，他完成了著名的土星光环研究，证明了光环不可能由固体或液体构成，而必须由无数小颗粒组成。这项研究为他赢得了亚当斯奖。1858年，他与凯瑟琳·玛丽·杜瓦结婚。在阿伯丁期间，麦克斯韦继续电磁学研究，发展了电磁场的概念，并提出了著名的'麦克斯韦妖'思想实验。然而，1860年马里沙尔学院与国王学院合并，他的职位被取消，这促使他转向研究工作，为后来在伦敦的突破奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1856, Maxwell was appointed Professor of Natural Philosophy at Marischal College in Aberdeen. Here, he completed his famous research on Saturn's rings, proving that the rings could not be solid or liquid but must consist of countless small particles. This research earned him the Adams Prize. In 1858, he married Katherine Mary Dewar. During his time in Aberdeen, Maxwell continued his electromagnetic research, developing the concept of the electromagnetic field and proposing the famous thought experiment 'Maxwell's demon.' However, in 1860, Marischal College merged with King's College, and his position was eliminated, prompting him to shift to research work, laying the foundation for his later breakthroughs in London.

points.title: 电磁理论大成
points.description: 1865年，麦克斯韦辞去伦敦国王学院的教职，回到苏格兰格伦莱尔庄园进行独立研究。这是他科学成就最辉煌的时期。他完成了电磁场理论的数学表述，提出了著名的麦克斯韦方程组，统一了电、磁、光现象。他预言了电磁波的存在，并计算出其传播速度等于光速，从而揭示了光的电磁本质。1871年，他回到剑桥大学担任第一任卡文迪许实验物理学教授，负责筹建卡文迪许实验室。在生命的最后几年，他继续完善电磁理论，并开始了气体动理论的研究。1879年11月5日，麦克斯韦因腹部癌症在剑桥去世，年仅48岁，但其科学成就影响了整个物理学的发展。
points.descriptionEn: In 1865, Maxwell resigned his professorship at King's College London and returned to his estate at Glenlair in Scotland for independent research. This was the most brilliant period of his scientific achievements. He completed the mathematical formulation of electromagnetic field theory, proposing the famous Maxwell's equations, which unified electricity, magnetism, and light phenomena. He predicted the existence of electromagnetic waves and calculated their propagation speed to be equal to the speed of light, thereby revealing the electromagnetic nature of light. In 1871, he returned to Cambridge University as the first Cavendish Professor of Experimental Physics, responsible for establishing the Cavendish Laboratory. In the final years of his life, he continued to refine electromagnetic theory and began research on kinetic theory of gases. On November 5, 1879, Maxwell died of abdominal cancer in Cambridge at the age of 48, but his scientific achievements influenced the development of physics as a whole.

supporter.zh: 麦克斯韦被尊为19世纪最伟大的物理学家之一，他的电磁理论统一了电、磁、光现象，是物理学史上最伟大的成就之一。支持者认为他不仅是一位理论物理学家，更是一位将数学与实验完美结合的科学大师。他的麦克斯韦方程组被誉为'物理学中最美的方程'，为现代电磁学奠定了基础。麦克斯韦的科学思想和方法论影响了爱因斯坦等后世科学家，他的工作直接导致了无线电、电视、雷达等现代通信技术的诞生，改变了人类文明进程。
supporter.en: Maxwell is revered as one of the greatest physicists of the 19th century. His electromagnetic theory unified electricity, magnetism, and light phenomena, standing as one of the greatest achievements in the history of physics. Supporters view him not only as a theoretical physicist but as a master who perfectly combined mathematics with experiment. His Maxwell's equations are hailed as 'the most beautiful equations in physics,' laying the foundation for modern electromagnetism. Maxwell's scientific thought and methodology influenced later scientists including Einstein, and his work directly led to the birth of modern communication technologies such as radio, television, and radar, changing the course of human civilization.

critic.zh: 批评者指出麦克斯韦的理论存在某些局限性，例如他的以太理论后来被证明是错误的。此外，他的数学表述虽然优美，但有时过于抽象，难以被同时代的科学家完全理解。麦克斯韦在气体动理论方面的工作虽然重要，但后来被玻尔兹曼和吉布斯等人超越。一些批评者还认为，麦克斯韦过于注重理论而忽视了实验验证，他的某些预测直到他去世后才被实验证实。这些批评者认为，尽管麦克斯韦的贡献巨大，但他并非完美的科学偶像，其理论体系也有历史局限性。
critic.en: Critics point out that Maxwell's theory had certain limitations, such as his ether theory, which was later proven incorrect. Additionally, while his mathematical formulations were elegant, they were sometimes too abstract to be fully understood by contemporary scientists. Maxwell's work on kinetic theory of gases, though important, was later surpassed by Boltzmann and Gibbs. Some critics also argue that Maxwell focused too much on theory while neglecting experimental verification, with some of his predictions only confirmed after his death. These critics suggest that despite Maxwell's monumental contributions, he was not a perfect scientific icon, and his theoretical system had historical limitations.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，麦克斯韦被视为经典物理学的集大成者，也是现代物理学的奠基人之一。他的电磁理论被认为是牛顿力学之后物理学最重要的理论突破，为爱因斯坦的相对论和量子力学的发展铺平了道路。麦克斯韦方程组被广泛认为是科学史上最优雅、最简洁的数学表述之一，体现了理论物理学的美学价值。在流行文化中，麦克斯韦常被描绘为典型的'天才科学家'形象，他的生平故事被用来激励年轻一代追求科学探索。他的名字被用于命名多种物理单位和现象，如'麦克斯韦'作为磁通量单位，体现了他在科学史上的不朽地位。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Maxwell is regarded as a culmination of classical physics and one of the founders of modern physics. His electromagnetic theory is considered the most important theoretical breakthrough in physics after Newtonian mechanics, paving the way for the development of Einstein's relativity and quantum mechanics. Maxwell's equations are widely regarded as one of the most elegant and concise mathematical formulations in scientific history, embodying the aesthetic value of theoretical physics. In popular culture, Maxwell is often depicted as a prototypical 'genius scientist,' with his life story used to inspire younger generations to pursue scientific exploration. His name is used to name various physical units and phenomena, such as 'maxwell' as a unit of magnetic flux, reflecting his immortal status in the history of science.

self.zh: 在科学中，当我们改变主题时，我们必须改变思想方式，就像我们改变工具一样。
self.en: In science, when we change the subject, we must change our way of thinking, just as we change our tools.

others.zh: 麦克斯韦的工作是自牛顿以来物理学中最深刻、最富有成果的工作。
others.en: Maxwell's work is the most profound and fruitful in physics since Newton.
